chunks: They solemnly swore by God with their strongest oaths: 'If a sign comes to us, we will certainly believe in it.' Tell them: 'The signs are with God.' Yet what makes you think that when they come, they will not believe?
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers say they would believe if they saw a sign, but God said they wouldn't?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological barrier of *istikbar* (arrogance) that prevents the disbelievers from recognizing truth even when presented with clear evidence, as their claim of conditional belief was often rhetorical rather than sincere. It underscores the divine wisdom in withholding immediate signs, illustrating that faith requires more than mere visual proof but a receptive heart free from stubbornness. This concept is central to the Shia understanding of the Imamate, where the presence of the Imam is the ultimate 'sign,' yet many fail to recognize him due to spiritual blindness.
